problem: C67 left cache-lock acquisition/map lookup and feature-GPU batch paths outside its terrain/cell-join attribution.
implementation: Test-only acquisition endpoints and inclusive map/feature-GPU API spans, with events appended after original guard release. Separate worker buffer reuses context, bounds, unions, failure evidence and cleanup. Production lock sequence and generation semantics remain unchanged.

design_review.scope: Test-only lookup and feature-GPU API attribution, layered on accepted C67; no production cache, scheduler, ordering or feature algorithm change.
design_review.production_diff: Original Mutex::lock Result is bound before the original map_err/entry/clone or run_batch expression. The temporary MutexGuard still drops at the original statement semicolon. Test-only finish runs after release; error strings and ? propagation remain unchanged.
measurement_contract: Acquisition timestamp is captured after lock() returns, retaining success/poison status. No collector append occurs while the observed mutex is held.

Inclusive lookup/call endpoint is captured after the same original guard release and before collector append. Acquisition is contained in lookup/call; overlapping kind totals are not wall-time shares.
Acquisition includes shard hashing, timestamp overhead and possible preemption; it is not kernel-blocked time. Inclusive map lookup also includes map work, allocations and Arc clone.
Separate Lookup buffer reuses physical-thread context validation, event bounds, unions and bounded task samples. Only scalar labels/endpoints are retained; candidates cannot move to another thread.
Failure/panic drops record abandoned calls, preserve acquisition success and restore outer task context. Root cleanup empties lookup buffers along with the existing task/join/terrain buffers.
Every lookup adds observer work and two raw events until the joined root summary. Overhead remains inside task/root/whole observer intervals, and observer timing is not ordinary performance.
Normal cfg(test) exclusion confirmed by release build and empty nm observer scan. Native library differs from C67, so no prior byte identity is claimed.

new_fixtures: Held memo shard and worker lookup, original value, poisoned cache error, interval nesting/union and buffer release
Nested panic, released poisoned lock, acquisition-success/call-failure distinction, missing-phase evidence and restored outer context

limitations: The held-shard fixture validates the synchronized release/result path; it does not impose a wall-duration threshold or prove scheduler dwell time.
Feature-GPU calls are covered but absent from all four measured Nether profiles. Other locks, including Planner::check, remain outside this buffer.
Host activity and observer overhead prevent quiet timing acceptance.

validation.comparison: Complete decompressed NBT and membership. Only MCA timestamps/compression representation excluded. Observer compares immutable original and actual C67; both ordinary variants additionally compare C68 observer. Repeated coordinates are not unique coverage.
validation.shader_readiness: Actual before/after status4 on every measured observer/paired region.
validation.initial_test_compile_failure: Test-only LookupCall re-export visibility failed compilation before tests ran; corrected in 989bd44. Initial and corrected logs preserved.

observer_cost.scope: Observer event volume and post-join summary overhead remain inside measured region. Host RSS sampled at five-second intervals is not exact peak or sustained memory acceptance. No ordinary timing or speedup claim.

interpretation: No feature_gpu_call events occur in any of the four measured Nether profiles. Optimizing this covered feature-noise GPU path cannot improve these particular runs; this does not rule out terrain GPU costs or other profiles.

Longest-task inclusive lookup medians: basalt blobs 5.32/6.25%, blackstone blobs 2.85/2.25%, brown mushroom 6.00/10.67%, large ancient debris 10.44/15.73% for standard seeds. Basalt pillar below 0.004% in both. These are within instrumented tasks, not whole-region shares.

Large outliers remain: basalt/blackstone longest-task maximum covered fractions exceed 99% on both seeds. Covered acquisition can include preemption and does not establish kernel-blocked duration or which owner held the mutex.

Custom/direct warped-fungi longest-task inclusive lookup medians 30.96/29.72%; boundary column-map acquisition medians 15.48/8.03%. Custom/direct twisting-vine lookup medians 15.43/17.80%. These paths warrant targeted investigation; separate medians and overlapping kinds must not be added.

The observer processes 1.9–3.5 million lookup events per typical Nether region; post-join summaries alone add median 718–1439 ms. Additional hot-path probe work remains inside task/evaluation timing. This is an expensive opt-in test diagnostic, not an ordinary benchmark.

Lookup coverage still excludes Planner::check, per-view cache locks, allocators and OS scheduling. Residual time remains unclassified. No general lock-free or scheduling rewrite is justified by these fractions alone.
decision: Select diagnostic-only coverage and exact-output proof. Quiet timing/no-regression confirmation is deferred by user. Normal observer symbols are absent, but hash differs from C67; no prior byte identity or speedup claimed. Actual merged rebuild/full corpus follows merge.
